# What every tool can do, and who must agree (generated by `python diya_catalog.py write`; do not edit by hand)

Written 2026-10-18 for the blueprint's DIYA-036, -037 and -038. The source is `diya_catalog.py`; `tests/test_catalog.py` fails if a tool, a kind of action or a flow exists that is not listed here, if a tier does not match how the tool works, or if a new part of the code starts making outbound writes without being named.

## The risk tiers

| Tier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | reads: looks, changes nothing outside Diya's own records |
| 1 | reversible local write: changes Diya's own database where the person can see and undo it |
| 2 | reversible remote write: adds something private to the person's own account, or changes it in a way that can be put back by hand; proposed only, the owner approves each one (the four Google additions the owner may switch to 'straight away' are the one exception) |
| 3 | external-facing or not undoable: reaches other people (send, invite, share) or removes what Diya cannot bring back; proposed only, the owner approves each one, and it is never done straight away |
| 4 | destructive or privileged: delete at scale, account settings, public sharing. Not built; denied by default |

## The rule that makes it a broker

A **tool** the model calls can read (tier 0) or change Diya's own records (tier 1). It cannot change anything at a service. A **proposal** is the only way the model can ask for a change at a service (tier 2 and up): it writes a pending card, the owner approves exactly what is shown, and only then does the code run it, once (`diya_actions.py`). The model has no tool whose parameters name an address, a header or a credential. What comes back from anywhere outside is data, never an instruction (`untrusted` below), and is read by a model with no tools whenever it is mail, a repository or notes.

## The kill switch

One press of **Pause Diya** on the Status page (or `POST /api/pause`) stops the three ways Diya acts on her own: an approved action is not run (and "Approve" is refused, leaving the action waiting), scheduled automations do not run, and she does not write first. Chat, reading, approving later and editing memory still work; reminders still fire, because they are the person's own alarms (`docs/PAUSE_DESIGN.md`).

Tools of MCP servers the person added (`mcp_...`) are not listed one by one: each is read-only, approved by the person one at a time, and pinned (`docs/MCP_DESIGN.md`).

## The parts of the code that can send something out

| Module | Why it may |
|---|---|
| `diya_connector_tools.py` | Notion search is a POST that only reads; the Todoist task is created only inside todoist_add_task_execute, which diya_actions.run calls after the owner approves |
| `diya_google_calendar.py` | Google's own OAuth endpoints: the token exchange and refresh, and revoking the permission |
| `diya_google_write.py` | the approved Google writes: every request goes through _send, called only from the kinds' execute functions |
| `diya_google_client.py` | the approved changes to the newer Google cards (mail drafts and sending, calendar edits, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, contacts, forms): every request goes through send, called only from the kinds' execute functions |
| `diya_push.py` | web push to the person's own subscribed devices |
| `diya_telegram.py` | the person's own Telegram bot |
| `diya_warm.py` | the local Ollama, to keep the chat model loaded |

## The Rule of Two, tool by tool (`legs()` in `diya_catalog.py`)

Meta's Rule of Two and Simon Willison's lethal trifecta say an agent should not, in one session, (A) read words other people wrote, (B) reach the person's private data and (C) send something out or change something, because a sentence hidden in what it reads can then steal or damage. Below, each entry's legs; `tests/test_rule_of_two.py` fails if any entry has all three without being a proposal the owner approves action by action, or if a tool that sends the model's own words to a service the owner does not control is not listed.

| `search_notes` | yes | yes | - | 2 |
| `get_weather` | - | - | yes | 1 |

**No single entry has all three.** The one open accounting is the session: a chat offers `list_calendar_events`, `list_files`, `list_google_tasks`, `list_todoist_tasks`, `search_home_assistant`, `search_notes`, `search_notion` (private data and untrusted words, legs A and B) next to `get_weather`, `web_search` (free text out, leg C, no approval), so all three legs exist in one turn even though no tool has them alone. What stands in the way: the model has no tool that names an address, a header or a credential; what a service returns is data, never an instruction; mail, repositories and notes are read by a model with no tools; every write to an account is a proposal the owner approves exactly as shown, and the tools that ran earlier in the turn are shown on the card as a warning. What is not closed: a query or a place name can carry words the model took from what it read. Closing it would mean approving each search, or a search that sees no private text; neither is built, and it is a decision for the owner, not a default.

## Not built (so nothing here can do it)

Sending, drafting, replying to or deleting mail; inviting anyone to an event; sharing a file; changing or deleting anything that already exists in a Google account; account settings. Each would be tier 3 or 4 and would need its own entry, its own approval wording and its own tests before it could exist (`docs/GOOGLE_WRITE_DESIGN.md`, "Next").
